key_insight: This paper introduces SAW, a real-world benchmark that explicitly measures observer-centric (agent-relative) situated awareness—letting models reason about viewpoint, pose, and motion rather than only object-object relations.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal benchmarks emphasize environment-centric spatial relations and neglect observer-centric relationships that require reasoning relative to an agent's viewpoint, pose, and motion; SAW fills this evaluation gap.
method: Curate a real-world dataset focused on observer-centric annotations (viewpoint, pose, motion cues, and agent-relative relations).
Define tasks and evaluation protocols that test situated awareness (e.g., viewpoint-aware QA, action-inference, localization from agent pose, temporal reasoning).
Benchmark state-of-the-art multimodal foundation models to quantify gaps and provide diagnostics for improving agent-relative reasoning.
impact: Provides practitioners a targeted benchmark to train and evaluate models for real-world, agent-centered reasoning—critical for robotics, AR, and navigation systems. It highlights concrete failure modes and guides improvements in multimodal and embodied AI.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram contrasting environment-centric vs observer-centric relations (arrows showing agent viewpoint and object relations).
Annotated real-world image/sequence examples showing agent pose, gaze/motion vectors, and labeled observer-centric queries.
Bar/line chart comparing performance of existing MFMs on standard vs SAW tasks to visualize the performance gap.
Task flow infographic: dataset collection → annotation types → evaluation protocol → diagnostic outputs.
paper_title: Learning Situated Awareness in the Real World
paper_authors: Chuhan Li, Ruilin Han, Joy Hsu, Yongyuan Liang, Rajiv Dhawan
